paper: Hansen, Hartong, Obers — Action Principle for Newtonian Gravity (PRL 122, 061106, 2019; arXiv:1807.04765)
note: Five genuinely OPEN questions, i.e. not answered by the paper's derivations or by our replication. Grounded in the specific type-II TNC construction, the twistless-torsion condition, matter coupling, quantum corrections, and holographic/thermodynamic implications.

questions.q: Does the paper's covariant type-II TNC action actually reproduce the full first-post-Newtonian (1PN) sector of general relativity, or only the subset visible in a two-derivative type-II action?
questions.basis: The paper frames its formulation as 'post-Newtonian without a 1/c expansion' because the action tolerates non-closed τ (temporal torsion), which carries some gravitational-time-dilation content. However, the derivation exhibited only the closed-τ Newtonian limit (Poisson equation) — no non-static, non-trivial τ configuration is worked through in detail. The standard 1PN Lagrangian for compact binaries (Einstein–Infeld–Hoffmann) contains velocity-squared and gravitational-self-interaction terms whose full match against the type-II action has not been demonstrated. Our replication verified only the C3 static Poisson reduction.
next_steps: Pick a well-controlled 1PN test case (e.g., two-body Lagrangian at O(1/c²), or the precession of Mercury) and expand the type-II action around a slowly varying τ with |dτ|~v/c.
Match coefficient-by-coefficient against the known 1PN result; identify any missing PN interaction terms.
If systematic mismatches appear, characterize them as 'genuinely captured by type-II TNC' vs. 'requires further sectors' — this sharpens the physical scope of the paper's construction.

questions.q: Under what precise physical/geometrical conditions is the twistless-torsion condition (dτ ∧ τ = 0) dynamically enforced on-shell by the type-II TNC action, and what happens when it is violated?
questions.basis: The paper's action allows non-closed τ generically, and the Newtonian limit imposes dτ = 0 by hand for the static reduction (C3). Newton–Cartan literature identifies the intermediate 'twistless torsion' (TTNC) condition dτ ∧ τ = 0 as a natural geometric structure permitting an absolute time foliation. Whether the type-II EoMs (eqs. 16–21) select TTNC as a preferred branch, admit torsional solutions violating TTNC, or leave the condition unfixed, is not fully addressed. This directly bears on the paper's own claim to have escaped the Type-I obstruction.
next_steps: Analyze the τ-sector EoM (variation of eq. 12 wrt Φ̃/v̂) in a generic (non-flat) background.
Classify vacuum solutions by whether they satisfy: (a) dτ = 0 (Newtonian), (b) dτ ∧ τ = 0 (TTNC), (c) neither.
Determine whether TTNC-violating solutions are physical or gauge-artifact; if physical, describe an observable consequence.

questions.q: How does a standard non-relativistic quantum field theory — whose U(1) mass is a central charge of Bargmann — consistently couple to type-II TNC geometry, where the analogous generator N is non-central ([N, G_a] = T_a)?
questions.basis: Bargmann-covariant non-relativistic QFT (Schrödinger fields, superfluids, Newton-Cartan matter) crucially uses the centrality of the mass generator to define a global U(1)_M symmetry and its background gauge field (m_μ, the mass gauge field). In type-II TNC, N is non-central and mixes with T_a under boosts. The paper only exhibits the classical point-mass matter Lagrangian L_m = α e ρ with α = −(d−2)/2 and defers the general matter-coupling question to the companion paper arXiv:1905.13723. Whether a fully consistent quantum matter sector exists — with no anomaly obstructing the type-II gauge structure — is genuinely open.
next_steps: Write the linearised type-II TNC gauge transformations on a Schrödinger field ψ(t,x) and identify what replaces the standard U(1)_M phase.
Compute the Ward identities for the non-central N and check for anomaly cocycles at 1-loop (e.g., using a heat-kernel or dimensional-reduction approach).
If anomalies appear, determine whether they can be cancelled by counterterms in the geometric sector or whether they signal a fundamental obstruction.

questions.q: What are the loop-level quantum corrections to the type-II TNC action, and is the theory perturbatively renormalisable (or asymptotically safe) as a stand-alone quantum theory of Newtonian gravity in D=d+1?
questions.basis: The paper writes down a classical two-derivative action with a specific two-parameter (α, coupling to matter) content and derives EoMs. It does not analyze the theory quantum-mechanically. Non-relativistic gauge theories often behave better under RG flow than their relativistic counterparts (e.g., Hořava-Lifshitz gravity variants), but the type-II algebra is new, and its quantum status — beta functions, one-loop divergences, unitarity of graviton-like modes in the type-II gauge — is not established.
next_steps: Compute the propagator around the flat type-II TNC background from eq. (12), identifying physical vs. gauge degrees of freedom.
Perform a one-loop background-field calculation (perhaps at d=3) to check for divergences at two-derivative level; compare with counterterm structure.
Contrast with Hořava-Lifshitz results: is type-II TNC power-counting renormalisable, and if not, what higher-derivative extension makes it so?

questions.q: Does the type-II TNC action admit a holographic dual (in a Lifshitz / Schrödinger / non-relativistic AdS setting), and can one define a first-law of thermodynamics for the type-II analogues of black-hole horizons?
questions.basis: Newton–Cartan geometry has been argued to arise on the boundary of Lifshitz spacetimes (Christensen, Hartong, Obers, Rollier 2013; Hartong, Kiritsis, Obers 2014). The paper's type-II generalisation opens the question: which bulk gravity duals produce type-II TNC boundaries rather than type-I? Separately, on the type-II side, whether horizon-like solutions exist (killing-vector generated by H alone? by a combination with N?), and whether they satisfy an entropy/temperature relation obeying a first law, is unaddressed. Both directions probe the physical depth of the type-II construction beyond its ability to reproduce Poisson's equation.
next_steps: Repeat the boundary-Newton–Cartan derivation for Lifshitz backgrounds but permit non-central boundary mass generator; check whether type-II or a further generalisation arises.
Search for stationary axisymmetric solutions of the type-II EoMs (eqs. 16–21) with a Killing horizon; compute area, surface-gravity analog, and conserved charges (Komar-like integrals).

If a first law emerges, compare the entropy expression to the Wald entropy of the corresponding relativistic solution in the 1/c² expansion; a mismatch would highlight new non-relativistic thermodynamic content.
